newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse rebounds from four days of fall.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse rebounds from four days of fall.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange regained some of recent losses on Wednesday as it recovered from four days of correction, partly helped by a very strong dollar, traders said.
"The market's corrective sentiment seems to end and many began to buy," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings. However, he added, many major investors have not yet reentered the market.
The BUX index advanced 91.13 points to end at 5,578.58.
The market's bullish trend was led by sharply rising hotel firm Danubius, pharmaceuticals Richter and the most actively traded oil company MOL, Czipo said.
Danubius surged more than eight percent to a new record high of 6,615 forints on what traders explained by expectations of strong 1996 results.

"There are only three days left (until the February 15 deadline) to release their results, I think definitely this is the reason behind the rally," one trader said earlier. Danubius closed at 6,615, up 515.

Richter leapt a massive 555 forints to finish at 12,450 forints, below a new record high of 12,500, reached earlier during the session. The rally came after a 'hold' recommendation by CS First Boston and traders said Richter peaked on the back of good annual results released on Tuesday.
MOL which slid hundreds of forints in the past few days recovered and advanced to close at 3,115 forints, up 105.
Corporate results, released by retailer Aranypok, assets management company Pannon-Valto and textile industrial company Pannon-Flax, triggered mixed reaction.

Aranypok remained untraded, Pannon-Valto closed steady at 580 forints, while Pannon-Flax surged 20 percent to a year-high of 660 forints, triggering its suspension due to too rapid an intraday rise of 20 percent.
